Both web tools are hard-blocked in this session — not a network/DNS issue, a permission-gate issue. Here is exactly what happened and what I could and could not produce.

## 1. webfetch — exact error (every attempt, identical)

```
permission required but no prompt available for webfetch
```

Attempts made: the Wikipedia URL twice (different prompts), and a control request to `https://example.com` — all three returned the same string. The tool never reached the network; the harness refused the call because the tool needs an approval prompt and there is no interactive user to answer it (this is a non-interactive/subagent session).

## 2. websearch — exact error

```
permission required but no prompt available for websearch
```

Two queries tried: `List of county seats in Washington state` and a quoted variant with "land area square miles". Same error both times.

## 3. Fallback attempts (also blocked)

- `bash` (curl to the Wikipedia URL, and even `echo probe`): `permission required but no prompt available for bash`
- `read` / `glob` / `grep` **do** work, so I searched the local project for a cached copy of the page or table: no `.html`/`.md`/`.txt` files exist in the repo, and no cached county-seat data. The only local hits were prior session logs of this same GAIA question, which show the *earlier* run failing with the identical permission errors — i.e. no previously retrieved copy of the table exists on disk either.

## 4. What I can report reliably

## 5. What I cannot report — land areas and populations

**I have no land-area (sq mi / km²) or population figures to give you, and I will not invent them.** Precise per-city census land areas are exactly the kind of number where a plausible-looking guess (e.g. "Seattle ≈ 71.2 sq mi", "Cathlamet ≈ 1 sq mi") is unverifiable in this session and would corrupt the downstream GAIA answer, which needs official 2020-census values from data.census.gov — also unreachable here. The only thing I can say as an unverified lead, not as data: the largest-seat-by-land-area contest is among the big cities (Seattle / Spokane / Tacoma / Vancouver), and the smallest are the rural seats under ~2 sq mi (Ritzville, Pomeroy, Davenport, Republic, Cathlamet, Friday Harbor, South Bend) — so the extremes must be settled from the actual table, not from memory.

**To get the real table:** re-run this with `webfetch`/`websearch` pre-approved (or with `bash` allowed so `curl` can fetch the page), or drop the saved HTML of the Wikipedia page into `D:\GoatCode-ts\gaia\` — `read`/`grep` work fine and I can parse the full 39-row table with land areas and populations from a local file immediately.
